Belleville Wix Academy
Welcome to Our School
We are a vibrant and successful primary school which shares a unique bi-cultural community with École de Wix. We offer an English stream and a bilingual French/English stream from Reception to Year 6, and a Nursery which is taught in English.
School Tours
Come and visit us on one of our small group tours throughout the year.
Our Ofsted Report
In February 2025, we received the highest outcome possible (Outcome 2) from an 'ungraded' inspection. This means there is sufficient evidence to suggest that the school would be judged outstanding in a ‘graded’ inspection.
Admissions
To find out more about how to apply for our friendly and successful school with its unique bi-cultural community, please click here.

Belleville Wix Academy
Ethos, Values And Aims
Our School » Ethos, Values And Aims
Belleville Wix Academy is part of the Quality First Education Trust. The Trust's schools share a common drive for an excellent education for all.
Together, all the schools in the Q1E Trust:
Considerate: caring, polite, community, fairness and understanding, encouraging others Articulate: communication skills, listening, freedom of expression, expressing emotions and ideas Responsible: leadership, responsibility for self and others, teamwork Effort: participation, perseverance, resilience, willingness and desire to improve
For over 20 years Wix has shared its site with École de Wix, a French primary school which is an annexe of the Lycée Français Charles de Gaulle de Londres. Between us, we offer three streams onsite: the English Stream (run by Belleville Wix Academy); the French Stream (run by École de Wix) and the Bilingual Stream (run jointly by the two schools).
We aim to ensure that all children on site have routine and meaningful opportunities to play together, work together and learn from one another. All children eat together, wear the same uniform, and share playtimes with their peers. We value and cherish the rich mixture of cultures and world languages represented at Belleville Wix and are particularly proud of the bicultural spirit on site.

Belleville Wix Academy
Breakfast and After School Club
For our Parents / Carers » Breakfast and After School Club
Our Breakfast Club runs from 7.30am until 8.30am Monday - Friday BWA term time only and offers a healthy start to the morning with a nutritious breakfast and playtime with friends.
The Breakfast Club is supervised by school staff. It encourages good eating habits as well as providing a settling environment which helps children in the daily transition from home to school and ensures that they are ready to learn once the school day starts.
Procedure for booking
Please log into your schoolcomms account using the details you have supplied to the school and choose the option for Breakfast Club. All places must be booked and paid for in advance. This is non-refundable. If you need an emergency place, please call the BWA school office, 02072283055, before 3.00pm the day before to request a place and wait for confirmation of booking. If you would like to attend the Breakfast Club, you need to complete this form and return it to the school office on admin@bellevillewix.q1e.org.uk
£5 per session, per pupil.
Please note we are only able to offer this provision during BWA term dates only
Pupils will go to their classroom at 8.30am if this is the time their day starts. If your child has a later start time, please speak to the Headteacher of the school your child is registered with to ensure they are supervised.
Please note this menu is subject to change.
Pupils are expected to wash their hands in the outside sinks on arrival.
The After School Club is run by Premier education who provide a variety of activities for children to participate in. Please visit their website here to book your place.
Clubs run by outside providers have their own rates and you will pay them directly. Unfortunately the school office are unable to book these for you or take any payments for the provider.
Clubs that are run by the school do not incur any charges. All teacher-led after school provision this year will be learning support-focused and by invitation only. Parents will be contacted directly by the school about these sessions.

Extra-Curricular School Clubs
For our Parents / Carers » Extra-Curricular School Clubs
We are pleased to offer a wide range of before and after school clubs for our pupils. Some are run by the school, and some are run by external providers.
We know that there is a high demand for clubs and places get booked up quickly. We want to open the clubs to more pupils. This means that pupils who are eligible for Pupil Premium may sign up for a maximum of four free clubs and all other pupils may attend two free clubs. If a BWA club is cancelled, we will endeavour to inform you by sending a message on the school gateway.
Clubs for Autumn 2026 can be found here.
From September 2025, the Lycée asked the Quality First Education Trust to run the clubs that were previously run by Kidoloisirs. These clubs are available to book via Magic Booking

Belleville Wix Academy
Parent Partnership
For our Parents / Carers » Parent Partnership
Parent partnership is valued at BWA. We know the importance of working well with parents and carers because they are the first educators of their child and parent involvement matters.
We want our parents to be informed about what their child is being taught in school and how they might help support their child further at home. Parent workshops are offered throughout the year and we actively encourage parents to let us know what support would be helpful for them.
Teachers are available to speak with parents daily and a termly consultation is offered.
Home School Agreement
At Belleville Wix Academy we continually strive to provide the very best for your children. We are required by the Government to publish a Home-School Agreement that reflects:
We have tried to create an agreement that is readily accessible to parents, carers, staff and children, which reflects the school and its community.
We invite you to sign it and return it to the school office as soon as possible. It is your prerogative to decide whether you wish to sign the Agreement and we will ensure that no family or child is disadvantaged if they prefer not to.

Belleville Wix Academy
Attendance
For our Parents / Carers » Attendance
Regular attendance and punctuality are essential components of a child’s education. In order to make the most of the learning opportunities provided within school, children need to have the continuity of provision which consistent attendance allows. We are committed to working with our families to ensure every pupil reaches their full potential not only academically but also socially and emotionally though regular attendance at school. Our Attendance Policy sets out our expectations.
We expect all pupils to attend school every day and to be on time. Periods of absence and poor punctuality are disruptive to a child’s learning and send poor messages about the value of education. We ask parents and carers to support us in ensuring their pupils do not miss out through unnecessary absences.
All pupils’ attendance and punctuality is monitored. Any child who attends school less than 90% of the time is considered to be a Persistent Absentee and a referral to Educational Welfare will be made for them. Further information can be found in the Department for Education's Working together to improve school attendance guidance and Wandsworth Council's School Attendance Advice.
Celebrating good attendance and punctuality
At BWA we celebrate excellent attendance. At the end of every term pupils who have attended school every day receive a 100% badge to wear with pride on their uniform.
Bronze 100% Badge is awarded to pupils who have been in school every day for one term.
Silver 100% Badge is awarded to pupils who have been in school every day for two terms.
Gold 100% Badge is awarded to pupils who have been in school every day for the whole school year.
Punctuality is an important life skill. It is also polite. The school day start times are shared with families and are available here. Any pupil arriving 5 minutes after their allotted slot will be late and must enter the school building via the main office, with an adult. They will be recorded as being late after the close of morning register. Punctuality will be monitored.
Pupils who are consistently late are disrupting not only their own education but also that of the other pupils. If your child has a persistent late record, you will be asked to speak with the Headteacher, or Assistant Head to resolve the problem, but you can approach us at any time if you are having problems getting your child to school on time.
Absences If you know your child will be late or absent, for example due to a hospital appointment or school visit, please provide the office with the relevant appointment letter in advance of the absence. Letters regarding absence should be handed in to the office and not the class teacher. This will enable us to keep all documentation regarding your child’s absences on file. All absences not reported to the school will be recorded as unauthorised, until the reason for your child not being at school is established.
Please be advised that where possible doctors and dentists appointments are to be made outside of school hours or during school holidays.
Sickness Please report your child’s absence in person or by telephone to the School Office on 020 7228 3055 as early as possible and before 9.00am. Please refer to National Health Service guidance if you are unsure whether your child should remain at home. If your child has been physically sick, or had diarrhoea, then they should be kept off school for 48 hours.
Collection Arrangements It is essential that the school knows if there is any change in collection arrangements for your child. Please ring the School Office on 020 7228 3055 as soon as possible and before 2.30pm. If there are any last minute changes, e.g. someone other than the person known to staff is to collect your child at the end of the day. Calling before 2.30pm is important as it allows time for us to get messages to classrooms before the end of the day.
Holidays are expected to be taken during the school holidays and parents do not have a right to take their child out of school for holidays during term time. Exceptions may be made at the discretion of Headteacher.
All requests for absence are treated sympathetically and only in exceptional circumstances will they be approved. A Leave of Absence form should be completed in the case of any request for leave, including holidays and should be emailed, or handed in, to the School Office. Holidays during term time are not allowed and will be classified as unauthorised.
